title: $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ is the limit of its finite levels
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with ring of integers $\cO_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$, and
let $X$ be a scheme. For $n\ge1$ let $(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be the constant sheaf of rings on
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with value the finite ring $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$, and let
$(\cO_E/\pi_E^{n+1})_X\to(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be the reduction maps.

1. For a finite set $T$, the constant sheaf $T_X$ is represented by the $X$-scheme
   $\coprod_TX$. For the profinite set $\cO_E=\varprojlim_n\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ the pro-étale
   $X$-scheme
   $$
   X[\cO_E]=\varprojlim_n\coprod_{\cO_E/\pi_E^n}X
   $$
   of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] represents $\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ (limit
   of sheaves of sets).
2. The underlying sheaf of sets of $\cO_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\cO_E}$ is represented by
   $X[\cO_E]$.
3. Consequently there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of rings
   $\cO_{E,X}\cong\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, the limit being taken in sheaves of rings
   (equivalently, in sheaves of sets, with the induced ring structure).

proof.text: Put $Y_T=X[T]=\coprod_T X$ for finite $T$, using the terminal finite quotient $T\to T$ in [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Thus $Y_T$ is an object of the small pro-étale site. By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site], $H_T=h_{Y_T}$ is a sheaf. By [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen], a section $f\in H_T(U)$ is exactly a clopen decomposition $U=\coprod_{t\in T}U_t$, and on $U_t$ it is the constant section labelled $t$. The coprojections $X\to Y_T$ form a finite Zariski covering, hence a pro-étale covering by [sk-def-pe-site] (also for $T=\varnothing$, when this is the empty covering of the empty object). Base change of this covering along $f:U\to Y_T$ exists in the site and is a covering by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site]. Its members are exactly the clopen pieces $U_t=U\times_{Y_T}X$, so each $U_t$ is a site object and the family $\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ is a pro-étale covering. If $t\ne t'$, then $U_t\times_U U_{t'}=\varnothing$.

source.place: Step 1: finite constant sheaves; Groupoids Tag 03YW, example-constant-group

proof.text: Let $c$ send $t$ in the constant presheaf to the constant section of $H_T$. To verify that $(H_T,c)$ is its sheafification, let $G$ be any sheaf and $a$ any natural map from the constant presheaf to $G$. For $f:U\to Y_T$, glue $a_{U_t}(t)\in G(U_t)$ over the covering of Step 1. They agree on overlaps: on equal labels they are the same section, and on unequal labels the overlap is empty, where a sheaf has one section because the empty family covers the empty object. The glued section is natural in $U$, since pulling back the labelled pieces gives the labelled pieces for the restricted $f$. This gives $H_T\to G$ extending $a$. Every such extension has these restrictions on every $U_t$, so uniqueness follows from the sheaf condition. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], $H_T\cong T_X$. For $T=\varnothing$ sections exist only on $U=\varnothing$, and the same empty-cover argument applies. The identification sends a map of finite sets to the map of coproducts carrying its labelled summands identically to the corresponding summands.

source.place: Step 1: explicit sheafification universal property; Sites Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint

proof.text: Write $A_n=\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ and $S=\cO_E$. We first justify the displayed profinite presentation. The extended absolute value is nonarchimedean by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $r=|\pi_E|_E$ satisfies $0<r<1$, and its unit-times-uniformizer factorization shows $x\in\pi_E^n\cO_E$ exactly when $|x|_E\le r^n$. The rings $A_n$ are finite and their transition maps are surjective by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]. Given compatible residues $(b_n)$, choose lifts $a_n\in\cO_E$. For $m\ge n$ the difference $a_m-a_n$ belongs to $\pi_E^n\cO_E$, so $|a_m-a_n|_E\le r^n$; the sequence is Cauchy and converges to $a\in E$ by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete]. It lies in $\cO_E$: for sufficiently large $n$, $|a-a_n|_E\le1$, hence $|a|_E\le\max(|a-a_n|_E,|a_n|_E)\le1$. Fixing $n$ and passing to the limit in $|a_m-a_n|_E\le r^n$ gives $a-a_n\in\pi_E^n\cO_E$, so $a$ maps to every $b_n$. Uniqueness follows because an element in all $\pi_E^n\cO_E$ has absolute value at most every $r^n$ and hence is zero. These reduction maps are ring maps. Their fibres are cosets of the balls $\pi_E^n\cO_E$, which are open (the absolute values are the discrete powers of $r$); these balls form a neighbourhood basis of zero. Thus this bijection is a topological ring isomorphism $S\cong\varprojlim_n A_n$ with its finite discrete levels, verifying the presentation used in the statement. For compactness, [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact] makes $\prod_n A_n$ quasi-compact. The compatibility equations define a closed subset: failure of any one equation is an open cylinder. A cover of this closed subset extends to a cover of the product by adjoining its open complement, so it has a finite subcover. The product is Hausdorff because distinct tuples differ in one finite discrete coordinate, and its cylinders are clopen; the same holds for the inverse limit. Thus $S$ is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected, as required for a profinite test object. This sequence is cofinal among the finite continuous quotients of $S$: the fibres of any such quotient are finitely many clopen sets. For each point choose a cylinder neighbourhood contained in its fibre; compactness gives finitely many such cylinders. Choose a level $n$ at least as large as their levels. Equality at level $n$ then forces equality under the quotient map, so the quotient factors uniquely through the surjection $S\to A_n$. Consequently [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] gives $X[S]=\varprojlim_nY_{A_n}$ with the reduction transitions. For every site object $U$, the universal property of this scheme limit gives $\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,X[S])\cong\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,Y_{A_n})$. Substitute Step 2. The index category $\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{op}$ is small, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] identifies the right side with $(\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X)(U)$. Subcanonicity [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site] makes the left side a sheaf. This proves clause (1), naturally in all reduction projections.

source.place: Step 2: limits of representables; Sites Tag 00W2, lemma-limit-sheaf; compactness: Topology Tag 08ZU (theorem-tychonov)

proof.text: Work with small skeletons in the larger sheaf universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. The functor $u$ in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] preserves finite limits and covers. Its composite $u_X$ with base change along $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ also does, by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] (1); this composite is [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] supplies a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint $L$ on set sheaves to $RG(P)=G(X[P])$. For any profinite $P$ whose represented presheaf $h_P$ is a sheaf, and any sheaf $G$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] give $\operatorname{Hom}(Lh_P,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_P,RG)\cong RG(P)=G(X[P])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_{X[P]},G)$. The other representable is a sheaf by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site]. The displayed bijections are natural in $P$ and $G$. Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] to the opposite of the sheaf category to obtain the natural isomorphism $Lh_P\cong h_{X[P]}$. In particular this isomorphism carries $Lh_g$ to $h_{u_X(g)}$ for every continuous $g:P\to P'$. This is the representable-pullback argument of Stacks Tag 04D3, written here using existing adjunction and Yoneda nodes.

source.place: Step 3: representable pullback; Sites Tags 00WX (lemma-adjoint-sheaves), 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism), 04D3 (lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf); Categories Tag 001P

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects] and [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-group-ring-objects] to $L\dashv R$ from Step 4. They give the abelian and commutative-ring inverse images with underlying set functor $L$, preserving the operations through the finite-product comparison. Their right adjoints are restriction $G\mapsto(P\mapsto G(X[P]))$. By [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], the prescribed abelian $p_X^*$ is a left adjoint to that same restriction; therefore the adjunction comparison identifies it with this lifted abelian inverse image. The canonical strong monoidal comparison is the one in [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]: multiplication after this comparison is induced by the pulled-back bilinear multiplication map. Hence the ring object of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] is precisely the ring obtained by applying $L$ to the set-level addition, zero, negation, multiplication and unit maps. For $S=\cO_E$, [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] says its underlying condensed set is $h_S$, with these pointwise operations. Step 4 now identifies the underlying set sheaf of $\cO_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\cO_E}$ with $h_{X[S]}$, proving clause (2).

source.place: Steps 3–4: compatibility of inverse images and ring transport; Sites Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi

proof.text: For each reduction $q_n:S\to A_n$, the naturality in Step 4 identifies its pulled-back map with the represented map $X[q_n]:X[S]\to Y_{A_n}$. Under Step 2, the ring operations on $Y_{A_n}$ are the finite-label operations: for $U\to Y_{A_n}$ and $U\to Y_{A_n}$, refine their two labelled clopen partitions by intersections, and on the part labelled $(a,b)$ addition has label $a+b$, multiplication has label $ab$, and negation has label $-a$; $0,1$ are the corresponding constant labels. The ring sheaf just described is the constant ring sheaf, not only a sheaf with the correct set sections: any map from the constant ring presheaf into a ring sheaf extends uniquely by the gluing of Step 2, and the same intersection refinement shows that this extension preserves addition, multiplication, negation and the constants. Thus it has the ring-sheafification universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The maps $q_n$ preserve all these operations. Step 5 therefore gives a cone of ring sheaves from $\cO_{E,X}$ to $(A_n)_X$ whose underlying set cone is the limit cone of Step 3. Its underlying set isomorphism respects all operations: composing either candidate operation with every projection gives the same finite-level operation, and the limit projections jointly distinguish sections. More explicitly, in the sectionwise limit $B(U)=\{(b_n):b_n\in(A_n)_X(U),\ b_{n+1}\bmod\pi_E^n=b_n\}$ define every ring operation coordinatewise. The ring identities hold coordinatewise; restrictions are ring maps; and a map into $B$ is a ring map exactly when all its projections are, by the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]. Thus this set-limit sheaf is also the limit in ring sheaves and the cone map from $\cO_{E,X}$ is a ring isomorphism. This proves clause (3), with the canonical reduction projections specifying the isomorphism.
